The Treutlen County Board of Commissioners is considering enacting an ordinance requested by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs and the Georgia Attorney General that local governments must adopt ordinances at least consistent with the Part V Environmental Planning Criteria to remain in compliance with the Georgia Planning Act of 1989. Adoption of a consistent Part V Environmental Planning Criteria ordinance is also a Minimum Planning Standard of the Heart of Georgia Altamaha Regional Commission’s Regional Plan, which all Heart of Georgia Altamaha Region local governments must meet to remain in good standing (and therefore eligible for many grant/loan programs) with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs. The public is welcome to obtain a copy of the ordinance from the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners office. The Treutlen County Board of Commissioners will not take any action on the proposed ordinance prior to its scheduled April meeting.

Treutlen County

From: Michelle Brown <brown@hogarc.org>

Sent: Wednesday, December 13, 2017 4:11 PM

To: Lance Hooks; Lois Byrd

Cc: Brett Manning; Rafael C. Nail; James Pope

Subject: Treutlen County Draft Environmental Conservation Ordinance Attachments: Treutlen County Draft Environmental Ord..doc

Lance/Lois:

Attached is our model “Environmental Conservation, On-Site Sewage Management, and Permit Ordinance,” which has been modified for your jurisdiction. This ordinance addresses the so-called Part V Environmental Planning Criteria under the Georgia Planning Act of 1989, or more specifically for you, protected river corridors, groundwater recharge areas, and/or wetlands.

The Georgia Department of Community Affairs (DCA) and the Georgia Attorney General have ruled that local governments must adopt ordinances at least consistent with the Part V Environmental Planning Criteria to remain compliant with the Georgia Planning Act of 1989 (the same act requiring adoption of comprehensive plans). This ordinance accomplishes that. Adoption of a consistent Part V Environmental Planning Criteria ordinance is also a Minimum Planning Standard of the Heart of Georgia Altamaha Regional Commission’s Regional Plan, which all Heart of Georgia Altamaha Region local governments must meet to remain in good standing (and therefore eligible for many grant/loan programs) with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs.

Please adopt this ordinance at your earliest convenience. Most of the Heart of Georgia Altamaha Regional Commission local governments have already adopted an earlier version of this ordinance around the year 2000. Your government fell through a time period crack when DCA and the Georgia Environmental Protection Division were considering changes (which never happened) to the Part V Environmental Planning Criteria. However, DCA now is requiring the Regional Commission to report (by March, 2018) on those governments compliant with the Part V Environmental Planning Criteria and the required Minimum Planning Standards. Thus, the new urgency for compliance and adoption of this implementing consistent “Environment Conservation...Ordinance” results.

Again, please adopt this ordinance at your earliest convenience to remain compliant with the Georgia Planning Act of 1989. It is a minimal ordinance with little effect unless something proposed is within 100 feet of a protected river corridor, looks to locate a septic tank in a groundwater recharge area, or would be located in an identified wetland. Please call if you have any questions.

Once you have adopted the ordinance, please send (by fax or email) a signed copy to our Baxley office so we can properly notify DCA of your compliance. You should fax it to (912) 367-3640 or email to brown@hogarc.org.

Thank you, Rafael C. Nail Assistant Executive Director/Planning Director

Michelle Brown Senior Secretary/Public Information Coordinator Heart of Georgia Altamaha Regional Commission
